images.caption: The site of the first integrated ironworks in North America. It was in operation 1646 to about 1670. It was founded by John Winthrop the Younger. The reconstruction of the site was made possible through an archeological dig at the site, historical documents as well as conjecture. In 1968 it was added to the National Park Service and named Saugus Iron Works National Historic Site.
images.alt: The site of the first integrated ironworks in North America. It was in operation 1646 to about 1670. It was founded by John Winthrop the Younger. images.filename: Gay Head clay cliffs 4 of town of Aquinnah, Martha's Vineyard, USA.JPG
images.caption: Martha's Vineyard's Gay Head clay cliffs - a piece of art over 100 million years in the making, are the end result of glacial deposits. According to local Native American Wampanoag myth and theology, these cliffs were considered sacred. The Wampanoag's major deity, Moshup, resided in these cliffs. Today, the use and protection of the cliffs and their clay is under the control of the local Wampanoag tribe in Aquinnah.

images.caption:
Comme à Québec la tour d'observation (Prudential Tower) est munie de vitre et il faut prendre la photo à travers un paquet de verre qui reflète la moindre lumière provenant de l'intérieur. Dans ce cas-ci, j'ai placé ma K-7 avec la pancake DA 21mm sur un mini trépied (Ultra-pod II) tout simple, le plus proche possible de la vitre. Mon Tilley a ensuite servi à couvrir les reflets. À voir large sur fond noir

The Prudential Tower has a magnificent view of Boston but you have to shoot through many layers of glass. I used my K-7 and a small pancake lens (DA 21mm f/3.2) on a small tripod (Ultra-pod II, the best 20$ I ever spent on a photographic equipment) as close as possible to the window. My Tilley was then used to cover the eventual reflections.See it large on a black background:
